history: A Veneto standard alongside the Aperol and Select versions. Cynar is bitter enough that it survives dilution better than either.
whyItWorks: Cynar’s vegetal bitterness reads as savory against the prosecco’s fruit, which is why it works before dinner where sweeter spritzes cloy.
steps: Fill a wine glass with ice.
Add the Cynar, then the prosecco, then the soda.
Stir once, gently. Garnish with an orange slice.
techniqueNotes: Build in that order—pouring sparkling wine last knocks the carbonation out.
3-2-1 by volume is the Venetian ratio: prosecco, amaro, soda.

substitutions.notes: Campari is brighter and more bitter; Aperol far sweeter.

name: Cynar Spritz
description: The artichoke amaro spritz—darker and more savory than an Aperol, and considerably less sweet.
